figures.finding: The Turks and Caicos Islands, a British overseas territory, does not take United Kingdom tax and levies no income tax of its own.

sources.said: 1.1 Tax Regimes The Turks and Caicos Islands has no direct taxation of any kind. … 1.3 Income Tax Planning The Turks and Caicos Islands does not have income tax.
Other than social security/national insurance payments, referred to in Section 6.6, there are no direct personal taxes in Turks and Caicos Islands (TCI).

figures.finding: The Turks and Caicos Islands levy no income tax or other direct personal tax; the only charge on pay is national insurance and national health insurance.

sources.said: 1.1 Tax Regimes The Turks and Caicos Islands has no direct taxation of any kind. … 1.3 Income Tax Planning The Turks and Caicos Islands does not have income tax.
Other than social security/national insurance payments, referred to in Section 6.6, there are no direct personal taxes in Turks and Caicos Islands (TCI).

figures.finding: National insurance was set to reach 12% of pay from 1 April 2024 (employer 6.5%, employee stated as 5.6%), on pay up to $4,000 a month, ignoring earnings under $108 a month; national health insurance adds 6% (3% each) on pay up to $7,800 a month with a $50 minimum monthly contribution. These figures come from a 2022 law-firm guide citing the Regulations.

sources.said: With effect from April 1, 2022, the total liability for national insurance contributions is equivalent to 10 percent (increasing to 11 percent effective April 1, 2023, and 12 percent effective April 1, 2024), apportioned between the employer and employee as follows: • employers are required to pay 5.5 percent (increasing to 6 percent effective April 1, 2023, and 6.5 percent effective April 1, 2024); • employees are required to pay 4.5 percent (increasing to 5 percent effective April 1, 2023, and 5.6 percent effective April 1, 2024). … For the purposes of the liability, there is a salary cap of 4,000 dollars per month. Earnings of an employee of less than 25 dollars per week, or 108 dollars per month, are ignored. … There is a total liability for national insurance contributions amounting to 6 percent (salary cap for purposes of liability, 7,800 dollars per month, but with a minimum monthly contribution of 50 dollars). Of that 6 percent, the employer and the employee pay 3 percent each.

figures.finding: No income tax is withheld; the employee's national insurance and national health insurance shares are withheld from pay and paid in with the employer's.

sources.said: The employee contribution to national insurance and national health insurance is withheld from salary and deposited directly into the relevant funds along with the employer’s contribution.

figures.finding: A non-resident performer, writer or director pays no income tax in the Turks and Caicos Islands.

sources.said: There are no residency rules for tax purposes as there are no direct personal taxes in TCI.

figures.finding: With no income tax, authors' fees and royalties are not taxed as income.

sources.said: The Turks and Caicos Islands does not have income tax.

figures.finding: There is no VAT or GST on a freelancer's fee.
figures.applies: Supplies in the Turks and Caicos Islands

sources.said: Value Added Tax (VAT) There is no VAT in TCI.
